name: ScreenLex
soft_passes: #3 concept 'cursor over framed window' is nameable but it's a 3-anchor cluster, no single clean silhouette
#5 passes only because the icon is wholly flat — no lighting to be inconsistent; zero native depth model
#6 reads as charcoal + blue + a traffic-light triad (borrowed chrome), but strictly exceeds <=2 hue families and reserves no accent for a focal element
#9 internally consistent flat vocabulary, but commits to no macOS era language at all
failures: #1 transparent background, no squircle field; corner brackets ~10px from edge would clip under the system mask
#2 no safe-zone margin (art to bbox edge x10-119); cursor pulls weight bottom-right, breaks optical centre
#4 three text lines + 3 dots + white-outlined cursor smear to mush at 16px; text already borderline at 128
#7 no field means contrast rides the wallpaper; pale blue card + faded text drop below 3:1 on light desktops
#10 not layered/appearance-aware; charcoal-on-light reading collapses in Dark/Clear/Tinted, no Icon Composer variants
#12 legible words baked into the card ('AI drives / efficie... / Human...') — load-bearing text that vanishes at Dock size
light_model: Flat — no directional lighting, no cast shadow, no specular or bevel. Only tonal cue is the card's faint top-lighter vertical gradient. Consistent by absence of lighting, not by a committed source.
devices: scanner viewfinder corner brackets (four-corner capture frame)
traffic-light mini-window showing real captured text
oversized macOS cursor as the fuse binding screen to action
rhymes_hint: flat web/SaaS + browser-extension utility marks — multi-object explanatory glyphs (viewfinder frame + mini-window + cursor) floated on transparency; the diagrammatic-productivity-utility family, not the Big-Sur single-object-on-gradient family nor the diagonal-tool (TextEdit/Preview) family
notes: Resolution: 128x128 ICO web render (favicon-grade), NOT the 1024 master; text/edges degraded, all hex from a 4x upscale so (estimated). Transparent background with art to the corners = either a genuinely non-native full-bleed-less icon or a favicon saved in place of the tile; nothing is designed for the macOS squircle. Traffic-light dots are borrowed macOS chrome. Cover.png reuses the exact scene beside a serif 'ScreenLex' wordmark on a Big-Sur-blue gradient wallpaper; icon's blue card = brand blue, so palette coherence is strong and deliberate. Subject (screenshot capture + OCR/translate + smart redaction) is communicated honestly, arguably over-crammed. Era-lag: a step further from native than the flat-Big-Sur laggards (agentpeek, 1password) — a transparent web-illustration mark; candidate for a 'non-native transparent web-mark' sub-family.
